title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 102: Statement to be annexed to notice

content.overview: Section 102 requires an explanatory statement containing material facts for each item of special business at a general meeting, including specified interests and information needed for members to understand and decide the business.
content.glance: For special business, attach material facts and disclose the specified interests of directors, manager, key managerial personnel and their relatives, plus information needed for an informed decision.
content.study:
## Material facts and interests
A statement setting out material facts concerning each item of special business at a general meeting must be annexed to the notice. It must state the nature of any financial or other concern or interest of each director and manager (if any), other key managerial personnel, and their relatives, and include other information and facts that enable members to understand the meaning, scope and implications of the business and decide on it.

## Business treated as special
Section 102 explains what counts as special business. At an AGM, business is generally special except the listed ordinary business, including consideration of financial statements and the Board’s and auditors’ reports, declaration of dividend, appointment of directors in place of those retiring, and appointment/remuneration of auditors as specified by the Act. At an EGM, all business is special. Read the full statutory list before classifying an item.

## Consequences and application limits
The section contains a consequence for non-disclosure/default and an exception framework for matters where the interest or benefit is not reasonably expected to be known to the promoter/director/manager/KMP. The precise current penalty and statutory exceptions should be checked against the current Act and applicable notifications before advice. Do not assume every AGM item needs an explanatory statement or that a generic statement satisfies the material-facts test.

sections.heading: Ordinary and special business
sections.body: Section 102 distinguishes ordinary AGM business from special business and treats all EGM business as special. Consult the complete statutory list before deciding whether an explanatory statement is required.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 102: Statement to be annexed to notice

examples.title: Adequate explanatory statement
examples.body: The notice for a special resolution includes material facts, the purpose and implications of the proposal, and the interests specified by section 102. Members receive the information the section requires for an informed decision.

examples.title: Material information omitted
examples.body: A notice attaches a statement but omits a director’s relevant interest or facts needed to understand the proposal’s implications. The mere presence of a document titled “explanatory statement” does not establish compliance.

hypotheticals.question: A company proposes special business at an EGM and attaches a short statement describing the resolution but omits a relevant director/KMP interest and the commercial implications. Is attachment alone sufficient?
hypotheticals.analysis: No conclusion follows merely from attachment. Compare the statement with section 102(1): material facts, specified interests and other information needed to understand meaning, scope and implications must be considered. Check the complete facts, any statutory exception and current penalty provisions separately.

distinctions.title: Section 102 and connected meeting-compliance requirements
